identity.title: New Measurements of the Radio Photosphere of Mira Based on Data from the JVLA and ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present new measurements of the millimeter wavelength continuum emission from the long period variable Mira ($o$ Ceti) at frequencies of 46 GHz, 96 GHz, and 229 GHz

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper we adopt a distance of 110$\pm$9 pc (Haniff et al. 1995), based on the period-luminosity relation of Feast et al. 1989.

distance_source.value: Haniff et al. 1995, from period-luminosity relation of Feast et al. 1989

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper we adopt a distance of 110$\pm$9 pc (Haniff et al. 1995), based on the period-luminosity relation of Feast et al. 1989.

question.value: Do JVLA and ALMA continuum data at 46, 96 and 229 GHz match the radio photosphere model of Mira A (size, shape, flux, brightness structure), and what are the properties of Mira B?

evidence.quote: The measured millimeter flux densities are consistent with a radio photosphere model derived from previous observations, where flux density $S_{\nu}\propto\nu^{1.86}$.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2011.0.00014.SV.

evidence.quote: ALMA observations of Mira were performed in Band 3 (94 GHz) on 2014 October 17 and 25 and in Band 6 (229 GHz)

findings_qualitative.value: Radio photosphere size decreases with increasing frequency, first observational confirmation for an AGB star

evidence.quote: this is the first time that this has been confirmed observationally for an AGB star

claims.hypothesis: Mira A flux densities follow the RM97 radio photosphere model
claims.experiment: Measure fluxes at 46, 96, 229 GHz and compare to S∝nu^1.86 at 110 pc
claims.finding: RM97 model supported and extended to higher frequencies

evidence.quote: We have found excellent agreement between the newly observed millimeter wavelength flux densities for Mira A and the radio photosphere model of RM97

claims.hypothesis: Mira A radio photosphere is resolved, with size decreasing at higher frequency and elongated

evidence.quote: The shape of the radio photosphere is found to be slightly elongated, with a flattening of $\sim$10-20%.

claims.hypothesis: Mira A surface is uniformly bright
claims.result: Uniform disk inadequate; disk+Gaussian fits best at 229 GHz

evidence.quote: the observed visibilities point to a nonuniform, asymmetric brightness distribution

claims.hypothesis: Mira B emission follows simple free-free spectrum
claims.result: Higher frequencies lie above prior relation

evidence.quote: imply that a more complex model is needed to fully describe the observed short-wavelength radio emission

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tidal distortion by Mira B insufficient to explain ellipticity (~5e-6)

evidence.quote: This implies an ellipticity $\epsilon\sim5\times10^{-6}$, several orders of magnitude smaller than observed.
